gaps.name: run
gaps.reason: The TUI runs in the integrated terminal; Mona's own turns use /v1. Opening the TUI is a deliberate user command, not an automatic fallback.

gaps.name: session-diagnostics
gaps.reason: Route is `codewhale sessions` then `codewhale session-diagnostics <jsonl>`. Neither Mona nor its smoke runs it, so no success is claimed.

gaps.name: scorecard
gaps.reason: Needs a metrics file to score. No native scorecard panel, and no sample input is invented; the cost lens shows recorded usage, not this quality score.

gaps.name: speech
gaps.reason: Paid TTS is outside 1.0 scope. The command is reachable in the terminal; Mona never calls it and never claims a configured route.

gaps.name: rc
gaps.reason: Upstream browser handoff; Mona does not depend on it. Reachable only as an explicit terminal command.

gaps.name: fork
gaps.reason: Thread forking has no native control. The terminal entry runs the CLI command, and a fork creates a new thread without workspace rollback.

gaps.name: init
gaps.reason: Writes a workspace file. The capability row prefills the exact command and never runs it automatically.

gaps.name: setup
gaps.reason: Writes configuration. Mona adds MCP servers through the engine's own route instead; `setup` is terminal-only.

gaps.name: remote-setup
gaps.reason: Cloud hosting is outside 1.0 scope. No remote is invented and no bundle is generated automatically.

gaps.name: workflow
gaps.reason: Checked-in JS workflows run through a Lane Runtime with no HTTP route, so Mona cannot launch or inspect them. A terminal entry would not fulfill MONA-019; full parity stays blocked until the engine exposes a route or Victor narrows scope.

gaps.name: lane
gaps.reason: Lane management is terminal-only on this build. Mona shows no lane control and does not simulate one.

gaps.name: review
gaps.reason: The billable model review is terminal-only; Mona's source review reads recorded turn artifacts and Git state instead, so no hidden model call happens.

gaps.name: apply
gaps.reason: Destructive and terminal-only. Mona's restore path is the engine's checked one-file file-revert (P13); no patch apply control is offered.

gaps.name: eval
gaps.reason: Terminal-only. Cost depends on the suite, so the row states that before invocation.

gaps.name: integrations
gaps.reason: Third-party harness integration is terminal-only; Mona makes no claim about a configured harness.

gaps.name: web
gaps.reason: The upstream browser client overlaps Mona. Reachable only as an explicit terminal command; Mona never opens it automatically.

gaps.name: login
gaps.reason: Credentials never cross the renderer. Provider keys use the dedicated P16 route; account login is terminal-only and user-initiated.

gaps.name: logout
gaps.reason: Destructive and terminal-only, with the engine's own confirmation. Mona does not offer a one-click credential wipe.

gaps.name: auth
gaps.reason: Provider keys are set through the engine's own route (P16); other auth modes are terminal-only.

gaps.name: account
gaps.reason: Local key routes remain primary; account status is terminal-only.

gaps.name: dispatch
gaps.reason: Cloud computers are unavailable. No control is shown and no remote is invented.

gaps.name: mcp-server
gaps.reason: Terminal-only. Mona is an MCP host, not a server; the row states the reverse direction.

gaps.name: thread
gaps.reason: Resume and fork flows are terminal-only beyond the studio's recorded resume.

gaps.name: sandbox
gaps.reason: The effective permission posture is shown from the turn receipt (P08), not recomputed here; `sandbox` is terminal-only.

gaps.name: update
gaps.reason: Mona never silently upgrades the engine. An engine change is an explicit, separately tested compatibility decision and stays terminal-only here.

gaps.name: Approvals bridge
gaps.reason: Verified: pending rows persist with the Runtime capability, both reply routes are wired (POST /v1/approvals/{id}, POST /v1/user-input/{thread}/{request}), and the engine's own thread-detail lists settle or expire them. Not verified: a live approval decision end to end, remembered grants (passed through, not listed), and clarifications on the tool-free compatibility transport.

gaps.name: Tool: apply_patch
gaps.reason: apply_patch is displayed as a tool-attributed change when the agent uses it. Mona offers no direct patch control.

gaps.name: Web search
gaps.reason: Web search is provider-native and may add provider charges. Mona makes no claim that a route has it enabled.

gaps.name: Terminal stream/input
gaps.reason: Engine terminal sessions can only be attached, never created (404 otherwise), so a client cannot open its own shell through them. Mona owns its PTY instead; an attach view for engine-owned shells is not built.

gaps.name: Workspace files, search, artifacts
gaps.reason: Project text search is P19. Mona never copies repository contents into its database to fake it.

gaps.name: Workspace snapshots/restore
gaps.reason: Whole-workspace restore (POST /v1/snapshots/{id}/restore) and forking patch-undo are not surfaced. A workspace-wide overwrite stays a separate, explicitly authorized action.

gaps.name: Engine update path
gaps.reason: Mona never upgrades the engine silently. The pinned 0.10.2 build is a tested compatibility decision; an upgrade needs a new qualification pass.

coverage.summary: 75 discovered rows: 43 verified, 28 open, 2 blocked gaps, 2 unavailable. 51 entry points exercised. Full parity is not claimed while any row is open or blocked.

drift.note: The installed engine matches the recorded surface.
